extracted.intended_audience: ALSC award and media-evaluation committee members / librarians serving on Caldecott, Newbery, Batchelder, Geisel, Sibert, Belpré, and similar committees
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and evaluative definitions governing committee member conduct, conflicts of interest, communication restrictions, and book/publication eligibility for ALSC award and medal committees (Caldecott and related committees). Includes definitions of publication terms and examples to guide eligibility determinations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality and communication about eligible titles
rubrics_metrics.description: Award committee members may not blog or otherwise communicate electronically (outside of the committee process) regarding any aspect of eligible titles during their term of service. At no time during or after their service may committee members discuss the status of books as having been or not having been a consideration, suggested, and/or nominated for the award.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Members must not discuss eligible titles in print or electronic media during their term. This prohibition extends beyond the term: members may never state whether a book was or was not considered. Exceptions/nuances (see 'When do I need to cease...' and Batchelder exceptions) apply. Violation risks compromising confidentiality of deliberations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Term start and resumption timing for public reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: ALSC policy indicates that you may not engage in print or electronic communication regarding eligible titles during your 'term of service,' which officially begins July 1 of your appointment year. If appointed after July 1, your term of service begins immediately.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Once the committee's selections have been announced at the LibLearnX Youth Media Awards Press Conference, members may resume bylined reviews, articles, and blogging even though the term officially ends at the following Annual Conference. The July 1 cut-off is used to cover galley-review situations because official publication dates can be delayed. Batchelder committee has exceptions allowing review of certain imports/translations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Galley/publication cutoff (July 1) guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Prohibition includes any and all new fall publication books that would be reviewed in galley form. ALSC uses the July 1 cut-off date for books in galley form to be safe and ensure consistency among committee members.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because official publication dates can be delayed such that a book could become eligible for the committee year, members should not review galleys produced after July 1. Example: a 2021 committee member could review any 2019 book in final form, but NOT any galleys produced after July 1.

rubrics_metrics.name: No serving in advisory capacity to trade publishers (teachers' guides/readers' guides)
rubrics_metrics.description: Policy does not permit members to write teachers’ guides or readers’ group guides for children’s trade-book publishers while serving on an award committee, as this falls under serving in an advisory capacity to a trade publisher.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If one wants to serve on an award committee, one must forgo writing these items during the term of committee service.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ordinary library reference assistance permitted
rubrics_metrics.description: Providing assistance as part of ordinary library reference duties does not disqualify a member from serving on an award committee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An author acknowledging reference help (e.g., research assistance during a phone call) is not considered serving in an advisory capacity that would create a conflict.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accepting appointment when a dedication occurs
rubrics_metrics.description: You may not accept an appointment if a children's book dedicated to you is eligible for consideration by your award or media evaluation committee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you learn of such a dedication once your term begins, you are expected to resign as soon as you find out.

rubrics_metrics.name: Close personal relationship definition (conflict of interest)
rubrics_metrics.description: A close personal relationship is defined as one that could reasonably be seen by an outsider as having an influence on your decision-making process; includes close friends and co-workers but not casual acquaintances (e.g., speakers at your library or people who sat next to you at dinner).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If in doubt about the degree of friendship, discuss specifics with the ALSC Executive Director. The test is objective: what an outsider might reasonably perceive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Immediate family definition for conflict rules
rubrics_metrics.description: For conflict-of-interest purposes, only parents, children, spouses, and partners must be included in the definition of 'immediate family.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Siblings and other relatives (cousins, etc.) fall outside this narrow definition; legal advice indicates immediate family ties are more susceptible to claims of conflict because they are likely to have stronger emotional and direct financial ties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accepting dinner invitations from publishers
rubrics_metrics.description: It is permissible to accept invitations from publishers to meal events and social gatherings at professional conferences, as long as they do not conflict with committee meetings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Committee members should be vigilant about maintaining confidentiality in these gatherings and may want to avoid talking about books; talking about non-book topics is recommended to relax while avoiding disclosure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of adult books not disqualifying
rubrics_metrics.description: Members who author an adult book scheduled for publication during their committee term are not disqualified from serving on a children's-book award committee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An adult book is ineligible for ALSC children's awards, so its publication does not create a conflict for committee service.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manuscript under contract is a conflict of interest
rubrics_metrics.description: If you have a manuscript for a children's book being considered by a publisher and it's under contract, members should avoid accepting appointment, because a manuscript under contract implies a financial tie to a publishing house.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Members must avoid any appearance of conflict of interest; if a manuscript is under contract, withdraw it temporarily if wanting to serve.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prior critique of an author's manuscript — evaluate publication likelihood
rubrics_metrics.description: If you previously critiqued a manuscript that might be published in your year of service, and there's a good chance it will be published during your committee year, it is best to decline an appointment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contact the ALSC Executive Director to discuss ways to verify a book's publication date if uncertain.

rubrics_metrics.name: Professional books about children's literature allowed
rubrics_metrics.description: Members are not disqualified from serving if they write, edit, or contribute to a book about children's literature that is aimed at professionals or other interested adults.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such professional/academic works are considered distinct from children's trade books and do not create conflicts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gathering external opinions — permitted with careful boundaries
rubrics_metrics.description: Committee members are strongly encouraged to speak with others (children and adults) regarding eligible books to inform themselves about varied perspectives, but must maintain confidentiality of committee proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When participating in verbal, in-person discussions, members should: practice active listening; ask open-ended questions; share only public information about award process/terms/criteria; keep personal comments minimal (especially negative ones); use sensitivity and positive frameworks; avoid publicly dismissing a book; try to avoid direct comparisons between two eligible titles; set context before discussing any title; and express only personal opinion using 'I' not 'we.' Chair or PCG should handle communications that might imply consideration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mock award discussions restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: Committee members are allowed and encouraged to participate in local book discussions (especially with children), but they must not participate in mock elections related to eligible titles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Members may observe mock discussions but should not discuss eligible titles or vote. If a member is required by employment to hold a mock election, discuss with the Chair to manage confidentiality.

rubrics_metrics.name: No disclosure of past committee deliberations
rubrics_metrics.description: Members who served on a past committee may discuss their own opinions of that year's books, but may not reveal details of other committee members' opinions or decision-making.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This rule preserves the freedom of committee members to speak candidly during deliberations, knowing their remarks will remain private.

rubrics_metrics.name: Four-year waiting period between service on specified committees
rubrics_metrics.description: There is a four-year waiting period between service on the Batchelder, Caldecott, Geisel, Newbery, Sibert, Legacy, or Notable Children’s Books Committees. The period begins from the last year of the term of service regardless of term length.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: a member serving on the 2018 Newbery Committee may not serve on any indicated committees until 2022. The ALSC Board allows operational practice to suspend the four-year period for emergency mid-year replacements. Appointment to a Chair position may occur within the four-year period for leadership needs; however, a prior Chair may not be appointed to a member position within the four-year period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'published simultaneously'
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Published simultaneously' means that a book was first published in the United States within the same calendar year that it was first published in any other country, whether or not the actual dates of publication are identical.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: If the U.S. and U.K. editions were jointly acquired and editorial work was joint, a few days' difference in release does not make it ineligible. But other issues (author residency, citizenship) may still affect eligibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'first published in the United States' / 'U.S. Publisher'
rubrics_metrics.description: 'First published in the United States' means the acquisition of the book and the editorial work were done by a publisher with editorial offices in the United States that publishes books under U.S. publishing conventions for a United States market.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A book may be eligible if published simultaneously in another country provided the acquisition and editorial work were done jointly or originated in the U.S. Publishers with primary editorial offices outside the U.S. but distribution/warehousing in the U.S. are excluded. Examples: Canadian publishers with U.S. offices are not considered U.S. publishers if editorial work is done at Canadian headquarters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'published' for eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Published' means prepared and issued for public sale. This includes acquisition, editorial work, and release of a book and may (or may not) also include marketing and promotion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The intent is that eligible books be available to the public; a book that is copyrighted but not yet published does not meet that requirement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication date vs. copyright date clarification
rubrics_metrics.description: If a book is published prior to its year of copyright as stated in the book, it shall be considered in its year of copyright. If a book is published after its year of copyright, it should be considered in the year of its publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The aim is to ensure every eligible book is considered but not in more than one year. Publication dates may initially be taken from the book, publisher's website, Library of Congress, or Amazon; verification should be done by Chair or PCG with ALSC staff if needed, not by individual members.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'Distributed' (for eligibility)
rubrics_metrics.description: Distributed means transmitted from the publisher to the wholesale or retail seller and may (or may not) also include marketing and promotion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to determine whether a book has been released for sale; examples include publishers' distribution arrangements (e.g., Publishers Group West).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'Editorial work' (for eligibility)
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Editorial work' means the negotiation process between author and editor that leads from initial manuscript to finished book; may include conversations, correspondence, written instructions, markings on drafts, or other communication about the book.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editorial work performed jointly by editors in different countries may make a book eligible under 'simultaneous' publication rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'Editorial office'
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Editorial office' means where 'editorial work' is officially done. The location refers to the business address at which such work originates; secondary or subsidiary offices are excluded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An office that only acquires or distributes the completed book is not an editorial office unless editing is done there. Editors working remotely do not change the business location determination; focus is on where the editorial work originates.

rubrics_metrics.name: American literature for children (origin-based definition)
rubrics_metrics.description: 'American Literature' refers to the origin of the book, not to where the action takes place or to characters. Origin is based on the author and publisher (e.g., American author and U.S. publisher).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: A book set in England can be eligible if the author is American and the publisher is U.S.-based.

rubrics_metrics.name: Original work requirement (not a re-creation)
rubrics_metrics.description: The intent is to ensure a book is a NEW creation and not a re-creation from some other work. No significant part of the book under consideration should have been originally part of another work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some minor portions previously published are acceptable, but not substantial reuse. Where cases are unclear, the Chair should consult the PGC and ALSC staff. Examples illustrate when new editions are ineligible (slightly recolored/reissued illustrations) versus eligible (entirely new illustrations).

rubrics_metrics.name: Young readers' editions derived from adult books are ineligible
rubrics_metrics.description: Children's books derived from previously published adult books, including young readers’ editions, are not eligible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This rule does not exclude works that create a new work based on earlier public-domain sources (e.g., adaptations from Shakespeare). Example: a young readers' edition that is substantially the same as an adult book would be ineligible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compilations/Anthologies are ineligible
rubrics_metrics.description: Anthologies and compilations of works by many authors are not eligible because they consist of multiple distinct elements and are not a unified single work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: a collection of short stories by different authors was ruled ineligible even if most authors were U.S. residents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Portion previously published elsewhere — minor portion allowed
rubrics_metrics.description: If a portion of a book was previously published elsewhere (magazine, collection, electronic), the amount previously published must be a minor portion; the substantial majority of the book must be wholly new and previously unpublished.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: a book containing one previously published chapter can still be eligible if that chapter is a minor part; substantially expanded works based on earlier articles may be eligible if most content is new.

rubrics_metrics.name: Traditional works eligibility (retellings)
rubrics_metrics.description: Books that are traditional in origin may be considered if the book is the result of original research and the retelling and interpretation are the writer’s own.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Original retellings of folk tales or traditional stories are eligible when the author creates a new version intended as a distinct book for children.

rubrics_metrics.name: Language requirement — In English
rubrics_metrics.description: Committee members should consider only books written and published in English. This requirement DOES NOT limit use of other-language words or phrases where appropriate in context.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Bilingual books may be considered, but award is given for the English text. If non-English text must be evaluated, the Chair may request a native speaker reader to assess whether flaws exist; outside readers should be told only that a book is 'eligible' and such contacts must be handled only by the Chair.
